sections.title: Imperialism, Fascism, and Culture
sections.description: This interdisciplinary graduate seminar will explore Marxist perspectives on imperialism and fascism, their interrelation and cultural dimensions, giving close attention to the work of intellectuals from the Global South. It will address foundational theories of imperialism, dependency, ideology, fascism, and cultural colonialism that were developed in the 19th and 20th centuries, as well as 21st century scholarship that addresses these phenomena in light of recent historical developments. We will also examine critical analyses of imperialism, (neo)fascism, and cultural struggle found in works of literature, theater, and film, as well as in texts, testimonios, and speeches of revolutionary leaders. We will take an international and historical materialist approach to analyzing fascism and its cognates (e.g. authoritarianism, neofascism), giving particular attention to post-WWII historical developments and the history of the Americas.
